strengths: Addresses a critical gap in VGM evaluation—existing benchmarks assess visual quality but not physical plausibility. This is essential for positioning VGMs as world models.

Novel physics-informed evaluation paradigm using conservation laws and governing equations rather than subjective judgments or trajectory matching. Overcomes fundamental limitations of trajectory-based metrics by accounting for unobserved parameters.
Comprehensive experimental design with 9 diverse physics experiments, multiple initial conditions, data augmentation, and evaluation of 6 state-of-the-art models on >9000 videos.
Rigorous methodology combining PINNs with conservation law validation, grounded by real-world videos as ground truth. Systematic analysis of failure modes (disappearance, duplicates, stillness).
Strong reproducibility: detailed experimental protocols, promised open-source release of code/data/leaderboard, and extensive appendices with implementation details and prompts.
Well-motivated and clearly presented, with effective visualizations (particularly Figure 1) that explain limitations of existing approaches and advantages of the proposed method.
weaknesses: Severely limited scope reduces generalizability: restricted to Newtonian mechanics in controlled lab settings, static camera, short clips, simplified assumptions (negligible air resistance/friction). These acknowledged limitations fundamentally restrict the benchmark's applicability to real-world scenarios.

Critical unresolved methodological issues: (1) Object mass estimation for energy conservation is not clearly explained but essential for correctness. (2) Time window selection for Physical Invariance Score is admittedly sensitive (10-25% range) without principled justification. (3) No validation that proposed metrics actually correlate with 'true' physical plausibility.

High discard rates (23-47%) across models complicate fair comparison—different models evaluated on different subsets of generated videos. Unclear whether low scores reflect poor physics understanding or generation quality failures, introducing confounding factors.

Somewhat predictable findings: the conclusion that visually-trained models struggle with physics is unsurprising. Limited mechanistic insight into why models fail or which physics principles are harder to learn. No investigation of potential solutions.

Insufficient statistical rigor: single generation runs per prompt with no confidence intervals, no significance tests, no inter-rater reliability metrics for dataset creation. 'Best of enhanced/plain prompt' selection risks cherry-picking favorable results.

Trajectory extraction fragility: depends on cascading vision models (SAM2, Depth Anything V2) with error propagation not quantified. 2D pixel coordinates without camera calibration introduce ambiguity. Smoothing operations could mask underlying issues.

Missing critical implementation details: mass estimation procedure unexplained; exact usage of depth estimates in scoring unclear; SAM2 annotation procedure not fully described. These gaps make reproduction difficult and raise questions about metric validity.

Limited validation of metrics: Eq. 24's normalization form S=1/(1+α·Cσ̄) lacks principled justification. Threshold in Eq. 25 appears arbitrary. No ablation studies on hyperparameters (PINN λ=1, window sizes, α value). Authors acknowledge some invariances are 'inherently easier to satisfy' but don't quantify this.

Incomplete baseline comparisons: Veo3 proprietary models excluded due to budget. No direct head-to-head evaluation of VLM-based or trajectory-matching baselines on identical test sets. Missing ablations on PINN architecture choices.

Scope limitations acknowledged but severe: Only 130 original videos in highly controlled settings. Small dataset by modern standards. Style transfer augmentation reuses identical physical content, limiting diversity. Extension to complex systems or uncontrolled real-world scenarios remains unclear.

strengths: Addresses a critical gap in VGM evaluation: assesses physical correctness rather than just visual plausibility, with clear relevance to embodied AI/robotics applications
Technically sound physics-informed metrics: PINNs to fit governing equations and conservation law checks are principled; real-world videos achieve 0.96-0.99 scores as upper bounds

Comprehensive validation: real-vs-real trajectory matching stress test (Table 7) demonstrates limitations of pixel-level comparison; extensive robustness analysis (noise, scale invariance, PINN architecture ablations)
Substantial real-world dataset: 130 videos with 10-20 repetitions, controlled variations, style transfer augmentation creates 10-fold diversity while preserving physics

Significant empirical findings: even SOTA models (Veo3, COSMOS) achieve only 0.60-0.66 scores; keyframe conditioning dominates (0.66 vs 0.50 single-frame); VLM evaluators unreliable (assigns 0% JPC to real projectiles)

Rigorous experimental analysis across 9 models with multiple conditioning modes; per-category breakdowns reveal model-specific blindspots (pendula harder than falling, open-source competitive with proprietary)
Transparent methodology: discard filter validated against humans (4.6% false positives), honest limitations discussion (Section 6, Appendix E), promised code/data release
Novel contribution: first benchmark combining physics-informed neural networks with conservation laws for VGM evaluation; curated real-world dataset is substantial effort
weaknesses: Limited scope reduces real-world applicability: only short clips (50-120 frames), controlled lab settings with fixed cameras; doesn't evaluate longer-horizon physical reasoning, unconstrained environments, or multi-object interactions beyond 2-body collisions

Physical assumptions not rigorously justified: claim that air resistance and friction are negligible relative to VGM violations is correlational not causal; spring experiment shows energy decay handled via ad-hoc 25% windowing; no quantitative analysis of dissipative forces impact

Trajectory extraction pipeline introduces potential failure modes: 2D-only (misses 3D effects), multi-stage process (segmentation→differentiation→smoothing→PINN fitting), high discard rates (23-50%) with ~17% false negatives could bias toward coherent motion generators

PINN evaluation has circular dependency: if trajectory fits poorly, unclear whether due to wrong dynamics or suboptimal PINN hyperparameters; manual specification of governing equations limits extensibility to unknown systems

Statistical reporting gaps: no confidence intervals despite 10-20 real-world repetitions per experiment; human alignment study uses only 42 videos with small per-category sample sizes; Spearman ρ=0.708 is moderate not overwhelming

Diagnostic tool without prescriptive guidance: identifies that models fail at physics but doesn't propose solutions (no exploration of physics-informed training losses, fine-tuning strategies, or hybrid approaches); limits impact on model development
Prompt engineering bias: different models use different upsamplers (ChatGLM vs proprietary); enhanced vs plain prompts show high variance in impact (+27.9% to -34.4%), creating potential confounds

Generalization questions unaddressed: findings limited to Newtonian mechanics in controlled settings; unclear whether results transfer to fluid dynamics, longer videos, unconstrained real-world scenarios, or other domains
